data.title: Fedora change aims for 99% package reproducibility
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Fedora项目正在努力实现99%软件包的可重现性构建，旨在确保给定相同的源代码、构建环境和指令，能够生成完全相同的二进制文件。尽管Fedora较晚开始这一工作，但其集中化的构建基础设施使得验证和追踪软件包变化更加容易。与Debian不同，Fedora的RPM格式在构建时嵌入了签名和构建时间等元数据，这导致无法完全实现"逐位"相同的重现性。Fedora因此提出了一种不同的定义，即只要软件包内容相同，忽略签名和部分元数据的差异，即可视为可重现。该提案得到了积极反馈，重点是如何实现这一目标，而不是是否应该进行。此外，文章还提到Fedora在XZ后门事件之前就已经开始关注供应链攻击的检测和缓解。openSUSE则通过设置固定的构建时间和主机信息来实现部分可重现性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：构建可重复性及其相关工具和实践

不同观点：
• [barotalomey] 对在项目中找到有价值的资源（朋友）表示感慨，分享了一个关于构建可重复性的GitHub链接。
• [froh] 对相关项目的参与表示赞赏，并分享了一个有关RBOS项目的新闻链接。
• [apatheticonion] 希望看到更多静态链接的二进制文件，例如Python的安装和使用非常麻烦。
• [nigel_doug] 质疑组织是否会因对源代码和二进制包的信任度低而采用适当的工件管理流程，尤其是在供应链攻击增加的情况下，是否会推动企业采用安全的工件扫描工具。

补充讨论：
• [nimish] 作为Fedora用户，质疑这种构建可重复性对个人的实际意义，尤其是对于隔离构建的理解需求。
• [kccqzy] 认为Haskell包在多线程编译时不可重现不是大问题，因为gcc编译器不支持多线程编译，并指出C语言世界中的并行性来自于并行编译多个翻译单元。
• [Dwedit] 指出可重复性与配置引导优化存在冲突，尤其是在涉及网络和其他不一致的IO时。
• [frainfreeze] 对可重复性进展表示赞赏，并分享了有关Debian bookworm live images现在完全可重复的新闻。
• [sheepscreek] 强烈希望有更多工具实现确定性，尤其希望能对Proxmox配置进行确定性处理。
• [kaelit] 对构建可重复性表示兴趣，提到正在构建与zk系统相关的内容，并表示后续会分享。

争议焦点：
• [trod1234] 对构建可重复性提出质疑，认为尽管在理论上相同的源代码、环境和指令应产生完全相同的二进制结果，但硬件特定的优化和硬件表现不一致性可能会破坏这种确定性。他认为现实中的硬件问题和抽象层次的复杂性使得构建可重复性难以实现。

总结：讨论围绕构建可重复性的价值、实现的难度及其在不同环境和工具中的应用展开。主要争议在于理论上的构建可重复性和现实硬件复杂性之间的差距。

Fedora change aims for 99% package reproducibility
Ready to give LWN a try?
With a subscription to LWN, you can stay current with what is happening in the Linux and free-software community and take advantage of subscriber-only site features.  We are pleased to offer you
a free trial subscription
, no credit card required, so that you can see for yourself.  Please, join us!
By
Joe Brockmeier
March 31, 2025
The effort to ensure that open-source software is
reproducible
has been
gathering steam over the years, and gaining traction with major Linux
distributions. Debian, for example, has been
working toward reproducible
builds
for more than a decade; it can
now
produce
official
live CDs
of the current stable release that are
reproducible. Fedora started on the path much later, but it has
progressed far enough that the project is now considering a
change
proposal
for the Fedora 43 development cycle, expected to be
released in October, with a goal of
making 99% of Fedora's package builds reproducible. So far, reaction
to the proposal seems favorable and focused primarily on how to
achieve the
goal—with
minimal pain for
packagers—rather
than whether to attempt it.
Defining reproducible builds
The Reproducible Builds project
defines
a
build as reproducible if "
given the same source code, build
environment and build instructions, any party can recreate bit-by-bit
identical copies of all specified artifacts
". In a
2023
hackfest report
, Zbigniew Jędrzejewski-Szmek said that Fedora has
not prioritized reproducible builds in the past because Fedora has
more control over its build process than Debian and other
distributions. Because Debian allows maintainers to
generate source packages on their local system and to upload
some locally built packages for distribution to users, he said that "
trust
in the contents of both source and binary packages is low
."
(Debian's build daemons build
most
binary packages from
source for distribution to users,
but
there are exceptions
.)
Fedora, on the other hand, exercises much more control over packages.
In Fedora, all packages that are distributed to users are built in the
centralized, strongly controlled infrastructure. All source rpms are
built from "dist-git": a git repository which contains the build
"recipe" and a cryptographic hash of package sources, so it is
relatively easy to verify what changed between package versions, what
"inputs" went into a particular source package, and in what
environment the binary packages were built.
However, even though Fedora has a tighter control over its
packages,
Jędrzejewski-Szmek
said that
one of the benefits of reproducible builds was to help detect and
mitigate any kind of supply-chain attack on Fedora's builders and
allow others to perform independent verification that the package
sources match the binaries that are delivered by Fedora. It's
interesting to note that Fedora had embarked on this work before
the XZ backdoor
drew even
more attention to supply-chain attacks.
He acknowledges that Debian is more advanced in its reproducible
builds processes, and notes that Fedora is setting a different
definition
for reproducible builds. This definition excludes signatures and
some metadata and focuses solely on the payload of packaged files in a given
RPM:
A build is reproducible if given the same source code, build
environment and build instructions, and metadata from the build
artifacts, any party can recreate copies of the artifacts that are
identical except for the signatures and parts of metadata.
The reason Fedora is pursuing a different definition of
reproducible build is that it
cannot
achieve "
bit-by-bit
" reproducibility by the
original definition. This is because of differences in the package
format and the way that Fedora builds its packages. RPMs embed the
package signature in the RPM when they are built, but Debian uses
detached signatures. RPMs also include information, such as the build
time (
BUILDTIME
) and build host (
BUILDHOST
) in the RPM's
header, that can affect reproducibilty. There was a
discussion
about allowing these variables to be overridden. However, the
prevailing opinion was that the information provided by
BUILDHOST
is useful, and
overriding its inclusion is not desirable. The contents, however,
should still be "
bit-by-bit
" identical, even though that phrase
does not turn up in Fedora's definition.
The openSUSE project, which also distributes software using the RPM
format, sets
BUILDHOST
to "
reproducible
",
according
to Jan Zerebecki. The actual build host is printed in the build logs,
and interested users can search openSUSE's build logs to find the
host.

data.title: Blue Prince is a roguelike puzzle masterpiece
data.author: adrianhon
data.article_summary: 《Blue Prince》是一款结合了roguelike机制与卓越艺术风格及故事叙述的原创益智游戏。玩家扮演已故富豪Herbert S. Sinclair的孙侄，目标是在庞大复杂的曼斯ion中找到第46号房间以继承全部财产。游戏采用5x9的房间网格布局，每次开门需从三个房间中选择一个加入探索，选择影响路线和工具获取。游戏没有跳跃惊吓、平台跳跃或时间压力，注重策略和房间布局规划。房间各具特色，包含逻辑和环境谜题，逐步增加难度。玩家需收集消耗品和永久道具，在资源耗尽或无路可走时游戏结束。整体氛围神秘，艺术表现精致，谜题设计独特且不重复。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：玩家对游戏《Blue Prince》的评价和争议

不同观点：
• **负面评价（throwerofstone）**：玩家认为游戏初期体验不错，但随后因重复的房间和资源获取机制变得乏味，尤其批评了RNG（随机数生成）机制，导致多次运行只遇到死胡同和重复的谜题，感觉游戏在浪费时间，特别不适合不喜欢 Roguelite 机制的玩家。

• **技术问题（tensility）**：玩家在M系列Mac设备上遇到无法运行的问题，验证文件后仍然无法解决，寻求帮助。

• **积极评价（galleywest200）**：玩家非常享受游戏体验，认为游戏的“元”谜题设计出色，推荐使用纸笔辅助游戏，并提到可以通过Gamepass等服务体验游戏以节省开支。

• **与其它游戏对比（npinsker）**：玩家提到游戏机制与桌游《Betrayal at House on the Hill》相似，认为该桌游甚至更糟糕，因为还包含属性升级，暗示《Blue Prince》的机制在同类中并非特别差。

• **对Roguelike与Roguelite的讨论（riffraff）**：玩家指出《Blue Prince》更像是Roguelite，因为有永久解锁的升级机制，而传统Roguelike游戏每次尝试都会清除所有进度。

• **独特性评价（nameless912）**：玩家认为《Blue Prince》是年度最佳 puzzle 游戏的有力竞争者，虽然可以与《Outer Wilds》或《Animal Well》比较，但实际上是独一无二的，特别强调纸笔在游戏中的必要性。

• **家庭游戏适合性（taeric）**：玩家考虑是否可以与孩子在晚上一起玩，类似于《Slay the Spire》的亲子体验。

• **游戏开发灵感（airstrike）**：玩家从《Blue Prince》获得灵感，想在业余时间开发类似Metroidvania风格的Roguelike游戏。

• **游戏体验不适（blindriver）**：玩家提到游戏的第一人称视角和移动导致晕动症，无法继续游玩，且无法退款。

• **游戏口碑（NelsonMinar）**：玩家提到《Blue Prince》在播客中获得高度评价，引用了Triple Click播客的讨论链接。

• **其他游戏推荐（billfruit）**：玩家提到另一款游戏《Dungeon of the Endless》，认为其开门/房间机制也非常有趣，特别是在紧张的游戏节奏下。

补充讨论：
• **技术支持与资源分享（zkiihne, davidpfarrell）**：有玩家提到与游戏相关的资源网站（mythicspoiler.com）和SteamGifts上的赠品信息。

• **平台兼容性问题（ndsipa_pomu）**：有玩家因为游戏不支持SteamDeck而决定不购买，强调多平台支持的重要性。

争议焦点：
• **RNG机制的合理性**：部分玩家认为游戏过度依赖RNG导致重复性高、体验不佳，而另一部分玩家则认为这是Roguelite游戏的常见特点，且有永久升级机制可以缓解重复性问题。
• **平台兼容性**：部分玩家对游戏不支持SteamDeck等平台表示不满，认为会影响其购买决策。

43628070.article_content:
Blue Prince is a Roguelike Puzzle Masterpiece
April 7, 2025
·
12 minutes
·
No comments
on Blue Prince is a Roguelike Puzzle Masterpiece
Playstation
,
Xbox
,
PC
,
Steam Deck
$29.99 (releasing April 10)
Dogubomb
Blue Prince
is a startlingly original puzzle game that marries compulsive
roguelike
mechanics with exceptional art and storytelling at an incredible scale. It begins with your arrival at the Mount Holly estate, a sprawling mansion owned by the late Herbert S. Sinclair. You’re his grandnephew and if you can find the 46th room of the building, you’ll receive it all.
Now, some will say you should play this game completely blind – in effect, that you should skip their review. It’s true that there is an intense delight in discovering the world and mechanics of Blue Prince, and if you want to preserve that in its entirety, you should return here later. But before you leave, I can reassure you of two things.
First, there are no jump scares or horror in Blue Prince. No twitch reflexes are required, nor any platforming, and there’s zero time pressure. To be fair, I’ve only played it for twenty hours; it’s possible these things might creep in later, but I really doubt it. Second, I won’t reveal any puzzle solutions, or anything from later in the game. I’ll be focusing on the game and puzzle design, and while I talk about the story in a general sense, that’s because it deserves critical appraisal. So with all that said…
Every game “run” concludes with your stats
The main activity in Blue Prince is exploring the mansion’s 5×9 grid of rooms. Every time you open a door, you have a choice of three rooms to “draft” – that is, to add to the mansion. Choosing a closet will offer two useful items but zero further exits, while a bedroom might offer one further exit and give you two additional “steps” (steps are consumed every time you move between rooms).
If you don’t like the look of your choices, too bad: you can’t back out after you’ve tried to open a door. The challenge, then, is drafting a network of rooms that gives you both the route and the tools to reach the antechamber to the 46th room, at the north end of the mansion.
Choices, choices…
There are many, many rooms to discover along the way, all gorgeously rendered in the game’s cel shaded art style and lushly filled with furniture and knick-knacks. Some are homely, some are grand, and some are positively eerie. Just wandering through the mansion is deeply atmospheric, the closest we’ve gotten to Susanna Clarke’s endless, shapeshifting world of
Piranesi
.
Rooms often have notes, pictures, and newspaper clippings. These are all illustrated beautifully, with spare yet crafted prose. This is not a hunt-the-object game where you poke through endless drawers and cupboards, though. Things you can collect or interact with are clearly marked, and paying attention is rewarded but not absolutely essential.
While rooms all have the same square footprint and are compact enough to be run through in a couple of seconds, they’re characterful and unique. Even identical copies of the same room “type” can look quite different depending on their placement in the mansion, their combinatorial possibilities reminiscent of the old
Hotel Magritte screensaver
.
Broadly speaking, there are two kinds of things to collect. The first are consumables: gold buys things from shops; keys unlock doors; gems draft special rooms (e.g. hallways with multiple exits); food grants extra steps; and dice refresh your choices of rooms to draft.
The second are items you can keep, like a spade for digging into piles of dirt that can contain useful things, or a sleeping mask that grants five additional steps every time you enter a new bedroom. Again, there are many, many items.
Find a magnifying glass and you’ll see a lot more…
Some rooms are explicitly marked out as containing puzzles: the parlour hosts a logic puzzle, while the billiard room has… something else. Solving them gives you a modest reward. The impressive thing is that these puzzles never seem to repeat and get slightly tougher every time you’re successful, to the point of becoming really quite tricky.
Rooms can also contain environmental puzzles: pulling levers on machinery, activating switches, and the like. These aren’t too hard providing you don’t overlook the instructions usually posted nearby, like I once did.
As you move further north into the mansion, things become trickier: more doors are locked, rooms seem to cost more gems, your step count dwindles. Drafting becomes an exercise in trade-offs: do you choose a room with certain rewards but heads in the wrong direction or a garden that’ll make future gardens cheaper to draft? These choices are influenced by your ever-changing situation: the chapel costs gold on every entry, but that’s not a problem if you have no money.
Eventually, you can’t continue. Sometimes it’s when you’ve run out of steps, but more often it’s because you’ve literally hit a dead end and there are no more doors to dr

• **家庭游戏适合性（taeric）**：玩家考虑是否可以与孩子在晚上一起玩，类似于《Slay the Spire》的亲子体验。

• **游戏开发灵感（airstrike）**：玩家从《Blue Prince》获得灵感，想在业余时间开发类似Metroidvania风格的Roguelike游戏。

• **游戏体验不适（blindriver）**：玩家提到游戏的第一人称视角和移动导致晕动症，无法继续游玩，且无法退款。

• **游戏口碑（NelsonMinar）**：玩家提到《Blue Prince》在播客中获得高度评价，引用了Triple Click播客的讨论链接。

• **其他游戏推荐（billfruit）**：玩家提到另一款游戏《Dungeon of the Endless》，认为其开门/房间机制也非常有趣，特别是在紧张的游戏节奏下。

补充讨论：
• **技术支持与资源分享（zkiihne, davidpfarrell）**：有玩家提到与游戏相关的资源网站（mythicspoiler.com）和SteamGifts上的赠品信息。

• **平台兼容性问题（ndsipa_pomu）**：有玩家因为游戏不支持SteamDeck而决定不购买，强调多平台支持的重要性。

争议焦点：
• **RNG机制的合理性**：部分玩家认为游戏过度依赖RNG导致重复性高、体验不佳，而另一部分玩家则认为这是Roguelite游戏的常见特点，且有永久升级机制可以缓解重复性问题。
• **平台兼容性**：部分玩家对游戏不支持SteamDeck等平台表示不满，认为会影响其购买决策。

不同观点：

• ** 主动沟通的重要性**：[bhasi] 分享了自己主动与老朋友沟通的经历，强调了脆弱和坦诚的对话可以加深友谊，否则可能会因为缺乏沟通而失去珍贵的友谊。
• ** 牺牲与信任的关系**：[w10-1] 提出相互的牺牲是信任的基础，如果一方在牺牲中感到被背叛，这种信任很难修复。即使是亲近的朋友或其他人际关系也如此。
• ** 自我价值与友谊**：[admiralrohan] 强调在交友之前，应该思考自己能给对方带来什么，无论是情感上还是物质上。如果自己生活中没有什么值得分享的东西，就很难吸引他人。
• ** 内向者交友的困难**：[MortyWaves] 指出内向者交友尤其困难，尤其是在频繁搬家或生活变动的情况下，且在线交友往往面临“幽灵”现象（即对方突然消失不回应）。

• ** 书籍参考**：[brianpan] 提到一本关于内向者尝试外向行为的书，提供了一种通过主动行动来改变交友模式的思路。

• ** 坦诚与好奇心的作用**：[Dansvidania] 强调了坦诚对话和好奇心在建立深厚友谊中的作用，认为不害怕展现脆弱和真诚的兴趣有助于建立长久的友谊。
• ** 通过技术促进联系**：[stroz] 提出了通过技术（如Soonly）来主动建立联系的思路，认为依靠偶然的社交机会不如主动创造联系。

Post 43: Intentionally Making Close Friends
Jun 28
Written By
Neel Nanda
Introduction
One of the greatest sources of joy in my life are my close friends. People who bring excitement and novelty into my life. Who expose me to new experiences, and ways of seeing the world. Who help me learn, point out my blind spots, and correct me when I am wrong. Who I can lean on when I need support, and who lean on me in turn. Friends who help me grow more into the kind of person I want to be.
I am especially grateful for this, because up until about 4 years ago, I didn’t have
any
close friends in my life. I had friends, but struggled to form real emotional connections. Moreover, it didn’t even occur to me that I
could
try to do this. It wasn’t that I knew how to form close friends but was too anxious to try, rather, ‘try to form close friendships’ was a
non-standard action
, something that never even crossed my mind. And one of my most life-changing experiments was realising that this was something I wanted, and actually trying to intentionally form close friends.
It’s easy to slip into a passive mindset here, to think of emotional connections as ‘something that take time’ or ‘need to happen naturally’. That to be intentional about things is ‘inauthentic’. I think this mindset is absolutely crazy. My close friendships are one of the most important components of my life happiness. Leaving it up to chance feels like passing up an incredible opportunity. As with all important things in life,
this can be optimised
- further, if done right, this adds a massive amount to the lives of me
and
of my future close friends.
The first half of this post is the story of how I approached intentionally forming close friends, and the second half is an attempt to distill the lessons I learned from this. As such, this post is more autobiographical than most. Feel free to skip to the advice section if you don’t want that. Further, what you value in close friendships is highly personal - this post will focus on what
I
want in friendships and how I try to get it, but you should adapt this to your own situation, values, and what feels missing in your life!
Exercise:
Think about your closest friends, and how these friendships happened. What needs are you fulfilling in each other’s lives? Are you happy with this state of affairs, or is something missing? What could be better?
My story
The Problem
Back when I was in school, I never had close friends. I had
friends
, people I liked, people I spent time with, whose company I genuinely enjoyed. But I was pretty terrible at being vulnerable and forming emotional connections. These friendships rarely went beyond the surface level. In hindsight, I expect these
could
have been far richer (and I’ve formed much stronger friendships with some of these friends since!), but I never really tried.
I find it hard to introspect on exactly what the internal experience of past Neel was like, but I think the core was that trying wasn’t
available
as a possible action. That I spent much of my life doing what felt socially conventional, normal and expected, for the role I saw myself in. And ‘go out of your way to form emotional connections’ wasn’t part of that. It wasn’t an action I considered, weighed up the costs and benefits, and decided against - it never even occurred to me to try. It didn’t feel like a void missing from my life - things just felt normal. It was like playing a video game, and having a list of actions to choose from, like ‘ask about their day’, ‘complain about a shared experience’ or ‘discuss something cool I learned recently’; but this list contained nothing about ‘intentionally form an emotional connection’. It wasn’t in my reference class of things I could do.
One of the core parts of my life philosophy now is the skill of
agency
, of
actually doing things
. The skill of going out of your way to
make
opportunities. To identify what’s missing in my life, and in the world. Finding the actions that I don’t
need
to take, that no one else will make me take, or do for me, and deciding to take them anyway. Fixing that which is broken. Finding that which is
not
broken, and deciding to make it better anyway. Exploring and trying new things. Challenging my self-image and growing. Fundamentally escaping the mindset of needing permission, and breaking past the
illusion of doing nothing
. I think this is one of the most valuable skills anyone can learn, and one I cherish, though I am far from perfect at it. And this experience is a large part of why I value it. Not realising I could make close friends was a
failure of agency
, an
unknown-unknown
that cut out a massive amount of potential happiness, without even realising it.
The solution
Despite all this talk of agency, I stumbled my way out of this problem pretty much by accident. When I was 18, in my final year in school, I ended up in a long-term romantic relationship (with a girl who, thankfully, was far better at taking initiative than me!). And this wa

data.title: AI Coding and the Peanut Butter and Jelly Problem
data.author: tylerg
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在理解和执行指令方面的能力，尤其是在编程、图像/视频处理等领域的应用和挑战，以及如何优化与LLM的沟通方式。

不同观点：
• **kenjackson** 认为LLM在理解文本指令方面表现优异，甚至优于人类，但在图像和视频生成方面远不如人类。他通过“项目管理秋千”故事类比说明问题，指出LLM在不同任务上的表现差异。

• **iDon** 强调了高层次语言和规范语言的长期梦想，认为我们正在进入一个新的阶段。他提到在提示（prompt）中清晰定义术语的重要性，并预测提示语言将进一步演变，类似于MCP成为连接LLM与其他应用的标准API。他还指出，过去的规范语言往往严格，因为其目的是生成可证明正确的代码，而提示语言可以更灵活地应用。

• **zahlman** 质疑如果一个人已经有能力清晰地沟通和定义需求，为何还需要AI来写代码。他认为，如果代码编写不简单，那么问题可能出在工具或架构上，而不是AI的价值。

• **Syzygies** 通过比喻说明AI工具的使用需要技巧和经验。他认为，虽然AI能极大地提高效率，但并不是每个人都能轻易学会如何最大化其潜力。他分享了自己在数学研究中使用AI编码的经验，认为理解代码仍是必要的。

• **daxfohl** 建议使用类似BASIC的协议来指导LLM，认为这样可以避免混淆英语和结构化编程概念，并且可以更灵活地调整和插入步骤，从而提高沟通的精确性。

补充讨论：
• **Peanut Butter and Jelly（花生酱和果冻）问题** 被多次提及，作为一个经典的指令执行和需求分析的教学例子。这个例子展示了清晰沟通和精确指令的重要性，并引发了关于如何有效与AI沟通的讨论。

• **争议焦点** 在于LLM在不同任务上的有效性和实际应用中的沟通挑战。部分评论者认为AI的价值在于其能够简化编码过程，而另一些人则质疑其必要性，尤其对于已经能清晰表达需求的人。

• **历史背景和教育** 提及花生酱和果冻问题在不同教育阶段的应用，显示了这一问题在计算机科学教育中的普遍性和持久性。

• **工具和语言演变** 一些评论者讨论了提示语言的演变和标准化需求，以及从历史编程语言（如BASIC）中汲取灵感来优化与LLM的交互方式。

data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: Google宣布其云部门将于第三季度允许客户在自己的数据中心运行Gemini人工智能模型。此举旨在吸引那些希望使用谷歌云技术同时控制自己数据的企业。相比之下，竞争对手Anthropic和OpenAI尚未开放其模型在物理数据中心的运行。Nvidia将为Google的Blackwell GPU提供Gemini模型支持，客户可通过谷歌或其他渠道购买这些芯片。谷歌还提到，即使是处理美国政府机密信息的企业也能通过隔离互联网的Google Distributed Cloud版本使用Gemini。2023年云基础设施市场总支出达1400亿美元，谷歌占有8%的市场份额。Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian强调，公司对多云环境和AI的投资吸引了大量客户。

Key Points
Google's cloud group will let companies run its Gemini artificial intelligence models in their own data centers starting in the third quarter.
Anthropic and OpenAI have yet to open up their models to run in physical data centers.

Thomas Kurian presents at the Google's I/O Developer's Conference in Mountain View, Calif, on May 10, 2023.
Courtesy: Google
Google's
cloud unit said Wednesday that clients will be able to run its Gemini artificial intelligence models in their own data centers.
Early access to Google Distributed Cloud will be available in the third quarter, Google said in a
blog post
. The service is targeted at clients that want to use Google's cloud technology while retaining control of their data.
As part of the announcement, Google said
Nvidia
will bring Gemini models to the company's Blackwell graphics processing units, or GPUs. Companies can buy the chips through Google or other channels.
OpenAI and Anthropic, two of Google's leading rivals in developing large language models, have shied away from providing access in physical data centers because it gives them less control over the quality and speed of the technology. Cohere
has an option
for customers to deploy models on their own infrastructure, but the AI startup says it's slower to set up than going through the company or using clouds.
Google's gesture may be attractive to a new set of potential customers. Many companies, schools and governments still maintain their own data center hardware, although cloud services have become common in recent years. Even customers that adhere to the secret and top secret U.S. government classification levels will be able to use Gemini through an air-gapped version of Google Distributed Cloud that's disconnected from the internet.
In 2023, cloud infrastructure spending totaled
$140 billion
, according to technology industry researcher Gartner. Google had 8% of the market in 2023, while
Amazon
controlled 39% and
Microsoft
held 23%, Gartner said. Last month, Google announced a
$32 billion agreement
to acquire cloud security startup Wiz.
"Our commitment to multi-cloud, along with our investments in infrastructure and in AI, are some of the reasons we're seeing tremendous movement with customers," Google Cloud chief Thomas Kurian said on a conference call after the Wiz announcement.
Google's Gemini models can process text, audio and video feeds, with support for more than 100 languages.

data.title: C++: terser (shorter) lambda == SHORTY (ab-use?)
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: `shorty` 是一个 C++ 库，旨在通过更简洁的语法来使用 lambda 表达式和函数操作，而不是替换 C++ 的核心功能。它提供了多种简化的操作符和函数调用方式，如使用 `$lhs`、`$rhs` 来处理排序条件，使用 `$i`、`$n` 等符号访问函数参数，以及通过 `$<callable>` 或 `$call<callable>` 调用可调用对象。此外，库支持元组操作、参数捕获、类型转换和赋值操作等功能，简化了代码书写。通过这些特性，开发者可以用更少的代码实现复杂的函数操作。库的实现依赖于 C++20 的 ranges 和 views 等现代特性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个C++库的实现及其语法设计的不同看法

不同观点：
• GrantMoyer：认为该实现简单直接，但不确定是否真的有用，特别是由于使用了Unicode名称（认为这是"被诅咒的"）。他提到实现中避免了复杂的成员调用语法。
• tempodox：持批评态度，认为C++已经有很多“黑魔法”了，而这个实现又增加了一层复杂性，特别是在模板错误信息的可读性上。
• mcdeltat：觉得这个实现很酷，并解释了非标准字符$在某些编译器中被接受的现象，指出使用$符号作为常量定义是合理的。
• gnulinux：虽然认为这个实现看起来很糟糕，但仍然对其表示喜爱，认为它类似于Boost Lambda2，并表示有兴趣尝试，但不会在生产环境中使用。
• hsfzxjy：认为这个实现看起来被“诅咒”，但从中了解到$符号可以用作标识符。
• notpushkin：表示欣赏，并提到这个实现让他想起了另一个类似的项目（dry-python/lambdas）。
• foxhill：最初对实现持怀疑态度，但后来有所改观，特别提到虽然美元符号语法不太理想，但整体还是有趣的。
• porridgeraisin：直接表示这个实现“令人惊恐”。
• pjmlp：从C++23的角度看不出这个实现有什么好处。
• pwdisswordfishz：认为这个实现类似于已经被淘汰的Boost.Lambda。
• nialv7：认为这并不是新概念，而是表达式模板的一种实现，并提供了维基百科的链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在使用$符号作为标识符的合理性以及整体实现的实用性和可读性上。
• 不同的评论者对这种“魔法”般的语法设计持有从欣赏到批评的不同态度，有些人认为它有趣且值得探索，而另一些人则认为它复杂且不必要。
• 一些评论者提到该实现与Boost Lambda或表达式模板的相似性，表明这种设计并非全新，但在某些方面有所改进或变化。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大学研究经费中的薪资分配与间接成本

不同观点：
• [pigmonkey] 认为俄勒冈大学的研究生每小时最低工资为24美元，外加全额学费、费用和健康保险，但工作时间限制在0.49 FTE。此外，间接成本用于支付设施租金、电脑、工资和行政费用，如撰写基金申请、遵守联邦法规等。他指出，15%的间接成本甚至不足以支付设施费用（如电费、设备维护等），而主要支出通常是主要研究人员的薪水，这些人的年薪可能超过15万美元。

• [musicale] 指出，研究生和博士后在大学研究基金中获得的报酬很少，通常只支付20小时的工作时间，而另外20多小时被视为“培训”且没有补偿。虽然学费和注册费可能由基金支付，但实际工作时间与报酬不匹配。

• [robwwilliams] 认为大学在间接成本上的收费过高，提到与ORNL合作时了解到大学支付的间接费用高达100%。他认为如果大学将间接费用降到15%会非常可笑，实际上不太可能发生。

• [TimorousBestie] 补充说，大学在间接成本上支付的比例已经算低的（60%），并暗示如果外界知道大学支付给承包商的综合费率，可能会更惊讶。

• [mistrial9] 分享了一个具体案例，提到某大学基金管理员拒绝让其他人访问数据库系统，导致不得不聘请他人来获取数据。该基金每年超过15万美元，但学生仅获得约10美元/小时的报酬，劳动成本远低于基金支付的总金额，且这种情况持续多年。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于研究生和博士后的薪资与实际工作时间是否匹配，以及大学在研究基金中的间接成本是否合理。
• 评论中还揭示了基金管理中的潜在问题，如不透明的数据库管理和过高的间接成本。

data.author: fmerian
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了使用SVG和CSS制作动画线条和遮罩效果的技术，特别是在React（JSX）环境中。文章首先展示了如何用`line`或`path`元素创建简单的线，并通过遮罩（mask）实现复杂效果。接着，文章讲解了如何为这些线条添加动画，并利用CSS的`@keyframes`实现位移动画。文章还提到如何使用SVG和CSS遮罩技术制作一个类似于Clerk风格的目录（TOC），包括在服务端渲染轮廓，并在客户端用SVG和CSS实现高亮部分的动画效果。最后，作者感谢了Clerk带来的灵感，并提供了React实现的源码示例。

关键技术包括：SVG、遮罩、CSS动画、React。

争议焦点：
• SVG在不同浏览器（尤其是Safari）中的兼容性和动画处理问题（braebo提出的SMIL问题）。

总结：评论者普遍认可SVG的强大功能和潜力，但也指出其在实际应用中的一些挑战，特别是在动画和跨工具兼容性方面。同时，评论中分享了多个实际项目和资源，为学习和应用SVG提供了丰富的参考。

Mask out an animated block, putting some animations and probably designed some parts in Figma or other SVG editors.

#
Clerk TOC
I made a clerk-like style Table Of Contents (TOC) on
Fumadocs
, you can try it out and play with the nice TOC.
To implement it, we have to render the TOC outline on server, without client-side JavaScript to make it compatible with SSR.
Since we're on server, we don't know the exact positions of elements.
My approach is to use
absolute
positions, render the outline as different "components", and snitch them together.
This isn't hard, but we also want to render a highlighted part of outline where the items are active, or their corresponding heading is visible in the viewport.
Like:
I'll call it the
thumb
. It has to be animated, so we can't just change the color of these outline components.
We cannot animate the thumb with simple CSS solutions, lucky we have the exact rendered positions of TOC items, since the thumb is meant to be interactive, it is
rendered on client!
Using the information from our browser, we can construct a "mask map" on client, look like this:
The method to construct this map is
SVG
- yes, our old friend.
<
svg
xmlns
=
"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
viewBox
=
"0 0 14 236"
>
<
path
d
=
"M1 0 L1 20 L13 36 L13 56 L1 72 L1 92 L13 108 L13 128 L1 144 L1 164 L1 180 L1 200 L13 216 L13 236"
stroke
=
"white"
strokeWidth
=
"1"
fill
=
"none"
/>
</
svg
>
The
d
property of SVG
<path />
isn't a nonsense auto-generated string, it's a list of commands.
See the
Web Docs
for more details, it's quite a powerful tool.
With our new tool, we can tell SVG to render a line connecting each point of the outline.
This constructed a SVG that's
identical
to our original TOC outline pre-rendered on server.
Similar to the technique we've learnt from Animated Wires, we can use the CSS
mask-image
property to mask an animated
div
block to render the thumb - a highlighted part of outline.
<
div
style
=
{{
maskImage:
`url("data:image/svg+xml,${
// URI encoded SVG image
encodeURIComponent
(
`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 236">...</svg>`
)
})`
,
}}
>
<
div
style
=
{{
width:
1
,
height: thumb.height,
transform:
`translateY(${
thumb
.
top
}px)`
,
transition:
"all 500ms"
,
backgroundColor:
"white"
,
}}
/>
</
div
>
Check the
source code
to see my implementation in React.js.
Huge thanks to Clerk for inspiring me on this, I've never thought the TOC of a documentation site can be that interesting to play with.

data.title: Tunarr: Create and configure live TV channels from media on your servers
data.author: Larrikin
data.article_summary: Tunarr是一款可以从Plex或Jellyfin服务器上的媒体创建直播电视频道的工具。用户可以通过其网页界面配置频道、节目、广告及相关设置。观看频道时，可以将伪装的Tunarr HDHomerun调谐器添加到Plex、Jellyfin或Emby中，或使用生成的M3U文件通过第三方IPTV播放器观看。Tunarr源于dizqueTV项目，但几乎完全重写，目标包括现代化技术栈、为现有用户提供迁移路径、稳定程序并修复漏洞、提升性能（目前使用Node 20.11.1开发和测试）、美化网页界面，以及添加大量新功能。

43665201.article_content:
Tunarr
¶
Create live TV channels from media on your Plex/Jellyfin servers, and more!
Configure your channels, programs, commercials, and settings using the Tunarr web UI.
Watch your channels by adding the spoofed Tunarr HDHomerun tuner to Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby. Or utilize generated M3U files with any 3rd party IPTV player app.
What is this?
¶
Tunarr was originally a fork of
dizqueTV
(which in itself was a fork of other projects!) which evolved into a near-complete rewrite. This project was born out of both a love for TV and an appreciation for the work put into dizqueTV and its predecessors.
Tunarr has the following goals:
Modernize the stack, both backend and frontend
Provide an
migration path
for existing users
Stabilize the program, fix bugs, and improve performance (Tunarr currently is developed and tested on Node 20.11.1, which offers
non-trivial performance improvements
over previous versions)
Modernize and "prettify" the Web UI
And of course,
Add a ton great new features!

KickSmash32
KickSmash32 is a Kickstart ROM replacement module for the Amiga 3000 and Amiga 4000 computer systems. There are other versions here for the Amiga 1200, 3000T, 4000T, and 4000CR. There is not yet a version for 16-bit Amigas such as the Amiga 500, 600, and 2000.
Features include:
In-system programming via an Amiga command line utility (smash)
Out-of-system programming (USB-C) via a Linux command line utility (hostsmash)
Up to 8 independent flash banks
Configurable ROM bank switching on long reboot or cold power-on
Optional host file service to the Amiga over the USB-C link (smashfs and smashftp)
All hardware, firmware, and software is open source.
View files in the doc directory for complete documentation.
Amiga CLI
The smash utility is used to interact with Kicksmash, including writing
Kickstart ROM images and switching to them. The smashftp program can be
used to transfer files with your host PC. The smashfs program will
automatically mount volumes exported from your host PC.
See
doc/AMIGACLI.md
for usage examples.
ROM Switcher
The ROM switcher is either a stand-alone ROM image or a Kickstart module
which, when linked with your favorite (3.1.4+ recommended) Kickstart image,
will provide a list of ROM images and allow you to pick which one to use.
It's recommended that you include the ROM switcher in your LongReset list.
See
doc/SWITCHER.md
for examples.
Development Environment
Instructions for building Kicksmash firmware, Amiga utilities,
and host programs are
available in doc/DEVENV.md
.
Which Kicksmash do I need?
Commodore produced a variety of Amiga machines over the years.
Unlike the Zorro slot, one thing that they did not standardize is the
location, orientation, and spacing of the ROM socket(s) in the machine.
Very few of the Amiga models have a compatible layout. In fact the only
two are the Amiga 3000 and the original Amiga 4000.
See doc/WHICH.md
for a guide on which KickSmash you
should choose based on your Amiga model.
Yes, there is FAQ
But it may not have the answers you seek. Check the doc directory
for additional information (any txt file). Here are some:

data.title: Air pollution fell substantially as Paris restricted car traffic
data.author: perihelions
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：巴黎减少汽车依赖和改善空气质量的措施及其效果

不同观点：
• **渐进式排放控制 vs. 全面禁车**：[bri3d] 认为巴黎通过禁止高排放柴油车（Crit’air 3, 4, 5）实现了空气质量的改善，而不一定是全面禁车。相较于限制车辆进入特定区域，减少高排放车辆的作用更大。[onlyrealcuzzo] 则质疑实际车辆减少的幅度，并提出是否是汽车排放技术改进带来的影响，而非单纯的政策措施。
  
• **政策效果的争议**：[onlyrealcuzzo] 对巴黎通过移除停车位、增加自行车道和绿地等政策所带来的实际效果持怀疑态度，认为数据可能夸大了汽车减少的实际情况。[HexPhantom] 则赞扬巴黎的执行力，认为尽管面临司机的反对，但数据证明了政策的效果，特别是在PM2.5和整体空气质量的改善上。

• **车辆类型的讨论**：[tom89999] 提到大型电动车虽然环保但占用资源的问题，指出其对城市空间的浪费。[mjevans] 提出一种折中方案，比如允许通过排放测试的低排放车辆或电动车行驶，并建议引入安静的市政车辆以减少噪音污染。

• **速度限制和交通工具选择**：[pluc] 提到英国在城市内采用20/30 mph限速，认为这有助于减少噪音和提高安全性。[bill38] 和 [codingclaws] 提到尽管巴黎在减少汽车依赖，但城市中仍有大量汽车和摩托车在行驶。[codingclaws] 还提到疫情期间的交通停滞导致空气质量改善的现象。

• **噪音污染的关注**：[jeffbee] 强调城市噪音问题，指出汽车是主要噪音源，并提到巴黎1995年和2025年的声音景观有显著变化。[grg0] 甚至认为城市围绕汽车设计是现代生活的悲剧之一。

补充讨论：
• **柴油车的依赖**：[whimsicalism] 提到欧洲对柴油车的依赖问题，并认为柴油车味道难闻，相比美国更为严重。
  
• **数据和研究的需求**：[tomtomistaken] 寻求关于城市NO2污染的长期数据集，并提到CAMS曾发布过相关数据，但已不再更新，显示了对更多数据和研究的需要。

争议焦点：
• **政策效果的真实性**：部分评论质疑巴黎空气质量改善是否完全归因于政策，还是由于技术进步或疫情等外部因素。
• **汽车限制的合理性**：关于是否应全面禁止汽车，或采取更折中的措施如限制排放，存在不同看法。

data.title: 'Paraparticles' Would Be a Third Kingdom of Quantum Particle
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了“准粒子”（paraparticles）作为量子粒子的第三种类型的新概念。在2021年，莱斯大学的研究生王志远在解决一个数学问题时意外发现了这种新粒子的可能性。这种粒子既不是物质粒子（费米子），也不是传递力的粒子（玻色子），而是具有隐藏量子态，并在两个粒子交换位置时发生变化。在王志远与其导师Kaden Hazzard进一步研究后，他们于2025年1月在《自然》期刊上发表了这一理论，提出准粒子可以存在并可能产生奇异的新材料。与此同时，维也纳的物理学家Markus Müller也在研究类似概念，探讨量子力学中多重现实视角切换的问题，进一步验证了准粒子的可能性。这两项研究的巧合让物理学界重新审视粒子种类的基本问题，探索我们的世界允许哪些类型的粒子存在。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [munchler] 对论文中提到的粒子性质表示疑惑，提出这些粒子是否是类似于电子"空穴"的准粒子，还是真实存在的粒子。他认为文章内容在此问题上显得矛盾。
• [whatshisface] 持乐观态度，认为如此简单的事物应该是真实的。
• [wizardforhire] 对该研究的发展表示期待，特别是对“收敛性”再次出现感到兴趣。

After he found an exotic solution, he started to wonder if the math could be interpreted physically. Eventually, he realized that it seemed to describe a new type of particle: one that’s neither a matter particle nor a force-carrying particle. It appeared to be something else altogether.
Wang was eager to develop the accidental discovery into a full theory of this third kind of particle. He brought the idea to
Kaden Hazzard
, his academic adviser.
“I said, I’m not sure I believe this can be true,” Hazzard recalled, “but if you really think it is, you should put all your time on this and drop everything else you’re working on.”
This January, Wang, now a postdoctoral researcher at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics in Germany, and Hazzard
published
their refined result in the journal
Nature
. They say that a third class of particles, called paraparticles, can indeed exist, and that these particles could produce strange new materials.
When the paper appeared,
Markus Müller
, a physicist at the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information in Vienna, was already contending with the notion of paraparticles for a different reason. According to quantum mechanics, an object or observer can be in multiple locations at once. Müller was thinking about how you can, on paper, switch between
the perspectives of observers
in these coexisting “branches” of reality. He realized that this came with new constraints on the possibility of paraparticles, and his team described their results in a
preprint
in February that’s now under review for publication in a journal.
The close timing of the two papers was a coincidence. But taken together, the work is reopening the case of a physics mystery that was believed to be solved decades ago. A basic question is being reevaluated: What kinds of particles does our world allow?
Hidden Worlds
All known elementary particles fall into one of two categories, and the two behave almost as opposites. There are the particles that make up matter, called fermions, and the particles that impart the fundamental forces, called bosons.
The defining characteristic of fermions is that if you switch the positions of two fermions, their quantum state gains a minus sign. The presence of that measly minus sign has enormous ramifications. It means that no two fermions can be in the same place at the same time. When packed together, fermions cannot be compressed past a certain point. This feature prevents matter from collapsing in on itself — it’s why the electrons in every atom exist in “shells.” Without this minus sign, we couldn’t exist.

This is what makes it possible to build lasers, which emit many identical light particles. This ability comes down to the fact that when two bosons swap places, their quantum state stays the same.
It’s not obvious that fermions and bosons should be the only two options.
That’s in part due to a fundamental feature of quantum theory: To calculate the probability of measuring a particle in any particular state, you have to take the mathematical description of that state and multiply it by itself. data.title: ArkType: Ergonomic TS validator 100x faster than Zod
data.author: nathan_phoenix
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了ArkType，一个针对TypeScript的高性能数据验证工具。它具有以下特点：

1. **即时反馈**：无需插件或构建步骤，每次按键都能获得类型级别的反馈。
2. **卓越的开发体验（DX）**：使用熟悉的语法，提供安全性和自动完成功能。
3. **更好的错误提示**：可深度定制的错误信息，默认设置良好。
4. **清晰简洁**：定义简洁，类型错误易读，悬停提示提供关键信息。
5. **高性能**：运行时比Zod快100倍，比Yup快2000倍，编辑器性能出色。
6. **深度内省**：利用集合论理解和暴露类型间的关系。
7. **内在优化**：每个模式被规范化为最纯净和最快的表示。
8. **全面的文档**：从安装到集成，提供所需的所有信息。

ArkType旨在提升TypeScript开发者的工作效率和体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ArkType与Zod等类型验证库的对比及其应用场景

不同观点：
• webdevladder认为ArkType不仅是一个模式验证库，还能将TypeScript类型带入运行时，提供更高保真度的类型操作能力。尽管Zod v4在性能和功能上有显著提升，但ArkType的更大 scope 和数据建模能力更吸引人，尽管其运行时代码体积较大，但通过预编译可能会改善。
• Aeolun对ArkType的 ergonomics 持怀疑态度，特别是对类型字符串化和双重类型编码表示不满，尽管ArkType速度快，但他认为速度并不是Zod的主要问题。
• Chyzwar简单提到Zod v4提升了性能，并提供相关链接。
• brap指出TypeScript的类型系统虽然强大，但缺乏运行时反射能力，导致需要像ArkType和Zod这样的库。
• alganet基于15年维护类似项目的经验，强调验证库的核心不在速度，而在于如何将模式树与错误报告树关联，并警告过度定制或限制会导致用户自行封装，从而影响性能和维护。
• madeofpalk表示对运行时验证兴趣不大，更关注构建时的模式验证，并认为生成代码验证工具是未来方向。
• t1amat认为Zod已成为标准，许多库依赖Zod模式，因此需要适配器来兼容ArkType。
• domoritz关心如何将现有TypeScript类型导入ArkType/Zod，并处理多种类型表示。
• tomaskafka分享了一个关于TypeScript类型无法在运行时验证的个人困惑，认为这是一个重大缺陷。
• chrisweekly将TypeScript与Sass类比，担心TypeScript的特性渗透到JavaScript中可能带来的影响。
• cendyne对如何实现类似ArkType的解析功能感兴趣，但TypeScript的类型推断速度慢阻碍了探索。
• cugul询问ArkType是否与华为的ArkTS有关，提供相关链接。

补充讨论：
• ArkType与Zod的性能和功能对比是讨论的焦点之一，特别是在运行时验证、ergonomics和代码体积方面。
• 关于验证库的核心价值和设计理念存在争议，特别是在速度与模式树和错误报告树的关联上。
• 对TypeScript类型在运行时验证的需求和工具支持的讨论，反映了对更强大类型系统的期望和现有工具的不足。
• 关于Zod作为标准和生态系统依赖的问题，提出了兼容性和适配器的需求。
• 最后，有人提到ArkType与华为ArkTS的可能关系，尽管链接内容未明确关联。

data.title: The AI magic behind Sphere's upcoming 'The Wizard of Oz' experience
data.author: radeeyate
data.article_summary: 《绿野仙踪》将通过AI技术在拉斯维加斯的Sphere场馆重现，这一项目由Google DeepMind和Google Cloud等多家公司合作完成。通过使用生成式AI模型（如Imagen和Veo），团队将1939年经典电影的原始素材转化为沉浸式体验，适应Sphere的16K LED大屏幕。由于传统CGI无法在成本和时间上实现这一目标，团队借助AI技术解决了放大画面、填补场景等问题，确保在不添加新对话和音乐的前提下，忠实再现原作。这一创新项目展示了AI在娱乐行业的突破性应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Sphere项目及其技术与艺术价值的争议

不同观点：
• [AIPedant] 认为Sphere项目将电影的艺术选择（如导演和剪辑）视为技术限制，迎合了追求内容而非艺术的文化。他们担心这种项目会破坏经典电影，如《Stalker》。
• [invisible] 则对该项目的技术实现表示赞赏，指出高生产价值的视频展示了出色的外绘技术、物理模拟和演员连续性，尽管存在一些视角和 lighting 问题。
• [sema4hacker] 关注项目的连续性错误，并引用视频指出了147个连续性错误，质疑项目在这些方面的改进。
• [actuallyalys] 对文章中暗示胶片电影低质量的观点表示不满，指出胶片可以扫描成高质量的4K视频，甚至更高，认为Sphere的16K分辨率需求更多是出于极端高分辨率，而非胶片本身的质量问题。
• [WalterBright] 从个人观影体验出发，希望通过AI技术改善无声电影的观看体验，包括去除颗粒感、增加音效、替换对话卡片、添加音乐和上色，认为这些技术可以让观众更好地享受老电影，而非忍受其局限性。

补充讨论：
• [imhoguy] 提出AI技术或许能让Jodorowsky的《Dune》改编最终实现，因为有足够的绘画材料可以喂给AI。
• [ge96] 提到NASCAR布局和Anema的电子舞曲风格跳跃，似乎与Sphere项目的技术讨论关系不大。
• [mrandish] 从技术和美学角度深入分析，认为Sphere项目在技术上和美学上都可能失败，特别是其极端的165度水平视野对导演和摄影师的创作选择造成了限制。他们指出，历史上超宽格式在电影叙事中的实验结果并不理想，并以Sphere展示的《Postcards from Earth》为例，说明其在故事和视觉呈现上的不足。
• [Xcelerate] 对Google DeepMind在亚特兰大开设办公室表示惊讶，认为这是一个值得关注的新闻。
• [leptons] 以幽默的方式质疑AI技术在电影中的应用，如Dorothy的手指数是否正确，暗示对AI细节处理能力的怀疑。

• Sphere项目是否破坏了电影的艺术价值，尤其是其对经典电影的重新制作和技术处理。
• 超宽视野技术在电影叙事中的适用性及其带来的技术挑战和观众体验问题。

The AI magic behind Sphere’s upcoming 'The Wizard of Oz' experience

How Google DeepMind and Google Cloud are helping to bring a cinema classic to larger-than-life in Las Vegas.
Matt A.V. Chaban
Keyword Contributor
Share
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Mail
Copy link
“The Wizard of Oz” may not be the first film shot in color, but many people remember it that way because of how director Victor Fleming cleverly used black-and-white film for the scenes set in Kansas.
Likewise, “The Wizard of Oz” may not be the first film to be reconceptualized with AI, but it may soon be known for that, too.
For months, thousands of researchers, programmers, visual effects artists, archivists and producers at Google DeepMind, Google Cloud, Sphere Studios, Magnopus, Warner Bros. Discovery and others in the film and technology industries have been working to bring the 1939 classic to a very big screen in a very big way.
On August 28, their work will debut at Sphere, the colossal Las Vegas venue that has been pioneering new forms of entertainment since it opened in September 2023. Now, generative AI will take center stage, alongside Dorothy, Toto and more munchkins than could ever fit in a multiplex.
It’s fitting that a work that once broke cinematic boundaries will do so again. “The Wizard of Oz at Sphere” is an equally epic undertaking of creativity and technology, where the story will envelop the venue’s 17,600-seat spherical space to create an immersive sensory experience.
Even a few years ago, such an undertaking would have been nearly impossible with conventional CGI. It’s really only become possible through the latest advances in generative AI media models,
specifically Imagen and Veo
, with
Gemini
also playing a major role. Not only does the team need to create an all-encompassing experience, but they also must do so with only the original material. Not a line of new dialogue was added nor a note of new music was sung in enriching this classic for Sphere.
“We talked about doing it in different ways,” says Jane Rosenthal, the Academy and Emmy Award-nominated producer who is a producer on “The Wizard of Oz at Sphere.” “We realized that we really needed to do it with AI.”
The wonderful wizards
Not that the team can simply enter a few AI prompts, click their collective heels and call it a day. Buzz Hays, the global lead for entertainment industry solutions at Google Cloud and a producer with 37 years in Hollywood, points out this is about more than using AI to expand an old film for a new format.
“We’re starting with the original four-by-three image on a 35mm piece of celluloid — it’s actually three separate, grainy film negatives; that’s how they shot Technicolor,” Hays says. “That obviously won’t work on a screen that is 160,000 square feet. So we’re working with Sphere Studios, Magnopus and visual effects artists around the world, alongside our AI models, to effectively bring the original characters and environments to life on a whole new canvas — creating an immersive entertainment experience that still respects the original in every way.”
When the project was first getting underway, there were many on the team, including within Google, who openly wondered if AI technology was there yet to complete the work or achieve the group’s collective vision. But because traditional CGI wouldn’t do the trick, at least not without massive expense and years of toil — and because everyone was excited to break new ground — they got to work.
“The models, they’re wildly innovative,” Dr. Steven Hickson, a Google DeepMind researcher on the project, says. “We’d find something we can't do, we think it's impossible, and then a month later we're like, actually, maybe we can do that.”
You can see why it seemed impossible, though.
Magnifying the original grainy images for Sphere’s 16K LED screen — the highest resolution screen in the world — was the first but far from the only challenge. The team also had to account for all the camera cuts in a traditional film that remove characters from parts of certain scenes, which wouldn’t work at the new, theatrical scale that was envisioned. Conventional CGI might have handled the scaling issue, but there are few ways it could fill out the rest of the scenes effectively.
Take the moment
where the Cowardly Lion first pounces
on his soon-to-be companions. The camera pans back and forth between the Scarecrow and Tin Man, with cuts to Dorothy hiding behind a tree in the distance. The experience at Sphere called for keeping all these elements together, in hyper-realistic detail.
To achieve this, the team has three major technical hurdles to overcome.
The magic of fine-tuning
Using versions of Veo, Imagen and Gemini specially tuned for the task, the Google teams and their partners developed an AI-based “super resolution” tool to turn those tiny celluloid frames from 1939 into ultra-ultra-high definition imagery that will pop inside Sph

data.title: Rebuilding Prime Video UI with Rust and WebAssembly
data.author: 8s2ngy
data.article_summary: Alexandru Ene介绍了如何使用Rust和WebAssembly重建Prime Video的用户界面，目标是客厅设备。作为亚马逊的首席工程师，Ene分享了重建过程中的挑战和技术细节。客厅设备如机顶盒、游戏主机和流媒体棒各有不同的性能和硬件能力，开发适配这些设备的UI非常复杂。为了解决性能问题并统一技术栈，团队使用Rust和WebAssembly重写了UI引擎，同时保留了业务代码使用React和JavaScript。新的Rust UI SDK提高了性能并简化了跨设备开发，但更新这些设备上的原生代码仍然是一个挑战。Ene还讨论了使用功能标志等方法处理硬件差异，并分享了经验教训。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TV应用程序的技术实现、用户体验问题、开源SDK的期望、技术选型的比较

不同观点：
• pmkary对该TV应用程序的表现表示惊讶和赞赏，虽然没有深入讨论技术细节，但明显持积极态度。

• badlibrarian指出该应用程序在配置较低的Roku设备上运行良好，但对需要为父母频繁更换更大电视以解决字体过小的问题表示不满。这里反映了用户体验中的实际问题，尤其是针对老年用户的字体设计。

• jackothy关注开发层面的问题，希望看到该应用程序的SDK开源，并指出该应用在技术上受到Leptos启发，但实际实现有很大不同，且包含许多有趣的功能。

• gozzoo对技术选型提出疑问，认为对于此类应用，Flutter可能比Rust和WebAssembly更合适，尤其是因为他对Rust和WebAssembly不太熟悉，反映了对技术适用性的不同看法。

• rgbrgb提出了一个具体的用户体验问题，即在Chrome浏览器中使用Prime视频播放器时，暂停后全屏模式下UI无法消失的潜在bug，质疑是否与该应用的UI设计有关。

• MeetingsBrowser表示不熟悉Prime的UI，但对使用该技术栈重建YouTube前端提出质疑，认为YouTube前端可能更适合这种技术实现，反映了不同应用场景下的技术适用性讨论。

补充讨论：
• 用户体验问题，特别是与字体大小和UI设计有关的实际使用困难，是讨论中的一个重要方面。
• 技术选型的争议，尤其是Rust和WebAssembly与Flutter的对比，反映了开发者社区对不同技术的偏好和适用性考虑。
• 对SDK开源的期望显示了部分用户对进一步开放和社区参与的兴趣。
• 具体的用户体验bug（如Prime视频播放器在Chrome中的UI问题）也引发了对应用稳定性和修复需求的关注。

Summary
Alexandru Ene features details of a new UI SDK in Rust for Prime Video that targets living room devices.
Bio
Alexandru Ene is a Principal Engineer in Prime Video at Amazon. Previously he’s worked in video games, game engines and has a passion for interactive media and high-performance systems.
About the conference
Software is changing the world. QCon San Francisco empowers software development by facilitating the spread of knowledge and innovation in the developer community. A practitioner-driven conference, QCon is designed for technical team leads, architects, engineering directors, and project managers who influence innovation in their teams.
INFOQ EVENTS
Apr 15th, 2025, 12 PM EDT
Architecting Scalable, Secure Multi-Agent Systems
Presented by: Michael Bachman - Head of Architecture and AI Strategy at Boomi
April 29-30, 2025, 9 AM PDT
API-First Innovation: Learn How Visa, DocuSign & Heineken Power AI Transformation
Register Now
May 1st, 2025, 11 AM EDT
Design Patterns for Agentic AI: Building Scalable, Event-Driven Systems
Presented by: Tyler Jewell - CEO at Akka and Richard Li - Founder at Amorphous Data
Transcript
Ene: We're going to talk about how we rebuilt a Prime Video UI for living room devices with Rust and WebAssembly, and the journey that got us there. I'm Alex. I've been a principal engineer with Amazon for about eight years. We've been working with Rust for a while actually in our tech stack for the clients. We had our low-level UI engine in WebAssembly and Rust for that log. Previously I worked on video games, game engines, interactive applications like that. I've quite a bit of experience in interactive applications.
Content
I'll talk about challenges in this space, because living room devices are things like set top boxes, gaming consoles, streaming sticks, TVs. People don't usually develop UIs for these devices, and they come with their own special set of challenges, so we're going to go through those. Then I'll show you how our architecture for the Prime Video App looked before we rewrote everything in Rust. We had a dual tech stack with the business code in React and JavaScript, and then low-level bits of the engine in Rust and WebAssembly, a bit of C++ in there as well. Then I'll show you some code with our new Rust UI SDK and how that looks, which is what we use right now in production. We're going to talk a little bit of how that code works with our low-level existing engine and how everything is organized. At the end, we're going to go a little bit to results, lessons learned.
Challenges In This Space
Living room devices, so as I said, these are gaming consoles, streaming sticks, set top boxes. They come with their own challenges, and some of them are obvious. There's performance differences that are huge. We're talking about a PlayStation 5 Pro, super nice gaming console, lots of power, but also a USB power streaming stick. Prime Video, we run the same application on all of these device types. Obviously, performance is really important for us. We can't quite have teams per device type, so one team that does set top boxes, then another team does gaming consoles, because then everything explodes. When you build a feature, you have to build it for everything. We were building things once and then deploying on all of these device categories here. We don't deploy this application that I'm talking about on mobile devices, like iPhone, iOS, mobile devices don't have this. This is just living room devices. Again, a huge range of performance. We're trying to write our code as optimal as possible.
Usually, high performant code is code that you compile natively. Let's say Rust compiled to native, C++ compiled to native, but that doesn't quite cut it in this space and we'll see why. Another pain point and challenge is hardware capabilities between these devices is a pain. As SDK developers, we need to think a lot about what are reasonable fallbacks that application developers who write the app code and the app behavior, they don't need to think about when they write that code and every little hardware difference. We try to have some reasonable defaults. That's not always possible, so we use patterns like feature flags and things like that to let them have a bit more control. It's a fairly challenging thing.
Another thing is we're trying to make this application as fast as possible with as many features as possible to every customer, but then updating native code on these device types is really hard. Part of that is these devices don't even have app stores, most of them. Maybe it goes up with a firmware update. That's a pain. It requires a manual process interacting with

data.title: Show HN: memEx, a personal knowledge base inspired by zettlekasten and org-mode
data.author: shibaobun
data.article_summary: **memEx** 是一个受 Zettlekasten 和 Org-mode 启发的结构化个人知识库工具。它支持多用户协作、隐私控制、跨设备访问以及双向链接等功能。主要功能包括笔记记录、上下文提供和流程文档化。安装可通过 Docker Compose 完成，配置包括主机URL、数据库连接、邮箱设置等环境变量。项目使用 AGPLv3 或更高版本许可，贡献和反馈可通过 Gitea、Weblate 等平台进行。

readme.md
memEx
A structured personal knowledge base, inspired by zettlekasten and org-mode.
Notes: Document notes about individual items or concepts
Contexts: Provide context around a single topic and hotlink to individual
concepts in your notes
Pipelines: Document your processes, attaching contexts to each step.
Features
Multi-user: Built with sharing and collaboration in mind
Privacy: Privacy controls on a per-note, context or pipeline basis
Convenient: Accessible from any internet-capable device
Backlinks: View referencing items from the referenced item
Installation
Install
Docker Compose
or alternatively
Docker Desktop
on your machine.
Copy the example
docker-compose.yml
. into your local machine where you want.
Bind mounts are created in the same directory by default.
Set the configuration variables in
docker-compose.yml
. You'll need to run
docker run -it shibaobun/memex /app/priv/random.sh
to generate a new
secret key base.
Use
docker-compose up
or
docker-compose up -d
to start the container!
The first created user will be created as an admin.
Configuration
You can use the following environment variables to configure memEx in
docker-compose.yml
.
HOST
: External url to generate links with. Must be set with your hosted
domain name! I.e.
memex.mywebsite.tld
PORT
: Internal port to bind to. Defaults to
4000
. Must be reverse proxied!
DATABASE_URL
: Controls the database url to connect to. Defaults to
ecto://postgres:postgres@memex-db/memex
.
ECTO_IPV6
: If set to
true
, Ecto should use ipv6 to connect to PostgreSQL.
Defaults to
false
.
POOL_SIZE
: Controls the pool size to use with PostgreSQL. Defaults to
10
.
SECRET_KEY_BASE
: Secret key base used to sign cookies. Must be generated
with
docker run -it shibaobun/memex priv/random.sh
and set for server to start.
REGISTRATION
: Controls if user sign-up should be invite only or set to
public. Set to
public
to enable public registration. Defaults to
invite
.
LOCALE
: Sets a custom default locale. Defaults to
en_US
.
SMTP_HOST
: The url for your SMTP email provider. Must be set
SMTP_PORT
: The port for your SMTP relay. Defaults to
587
.
SMTP_USERNAME
: The username for your SMTP relay. Must be set!
SMTP_PASSWORD
: The password for your SMTP relay. Must be set!
SMTP_SSL
: Set to
true
to enable SSL for emails. Defaults to
false
.
EMAIL_FROM
: Sets the sender email in sent emails. Defaults to
no-reply@HOST
where
HOST
was previously defined.
EMAIL_NAME
: Sets the sender name in sent emails. Defaults to "memEx".
Contribution
Contributions are greatly appreciated, no ability to code needed! You can browse
the
Contribution
Guide
to learn more.
I can be contacted at
shibao@bubbletea.dev
, or on
the fediverse at
@shibao@misskey.bubbletea.dev
. Thank
you!
License
memEx is licensed under AGPLv3 or later. A copy of the latest version of the
license can be found at
license.md
.

data.author: robenkleene
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Protesilaos Stavrou（又称“Prot”）撰写的《Emacs Lisp Elements》一书，该书提供了Emacs Lisp编程语言的整体视角。书中内容涵盖Emacs Lisp的基础入门、评估代码、缓冲区操作、符号与表达式、控制流和模式匹配等主题，旨在帮助读者通过编写Elisp来自定义和增强Emacs编辑器的功能。书中章节简明扼要，适合初学者和进阶用户，并鼓励读者在Emacs中实践书中的代码示例。书中还强调，学习Elisp不仅能提高效率，还能带来乐趣和成就感。本书并非Emacs Lisp的权威参考手册，而是一本实践指南，帮助读者快速上手并理解Emacs Lisp的核心概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs编辑器的使用体验、社区贡献、编程语言Emacs Lisp（Elisp）的特点以及Prot（Emacs包和主题的作者）的个人故事。

不同观点：
• [对Prot的个人看法和赞赏]
  - sauercrowd和NeutralForest都赞赏Prot不仅因为他在Emacs社区的贡献（维护Emacs包和主题），还因为他的个人生活选择——在经济困难的情况下自力更生，建造简陋的小屋，并通过YouTube记录和分享这一过程，展现了他的坚韧和灵感。
  
• [Emacs与LLMs的结合]
  - mark_l_watson提到，随着LLMs（大型语言模型）的兴起，Emacs可能会因为一些优秀的LLMs相关包而增加受欢迎度。他认为，尽管大多数人使用VSCode等编辑器，但Emacs在集成LLMs和工作流方面也有独特的优势。

• [Emacs Lisp的语言设计]
  - tikhonj分享了他对Emacs Lisp的长期使用体验，强调尽管Emacs Lisp违反了许多现代软件工程的“最佳实践”（如动态作用域、缺乏命名空间和静态类型），但它依然非常有效。他提出，成功的关键在于Emacs有一套小而富有表达力的核心概念，并且设计上高度一致，使得用户可以轻松理解和扩展它。
  
• [Emacs Lisp的不足与改进建议]
  - algo_lover指出，虽然`seq.el`的引入改善了对序列的操作，但Emacs社区仍缺乏现代数据结构库，尤其是对序列、alists和plists的整合不够便捷，限制了其易用性。
  - mijoharas补充提到，希望有更多关于关键字、alists/plists以及不同参数列表的讨论，因为这些是Elisp中常见的功能，但往往缺乏详细介绍。

• [对文档的看法]
  - ajross认为，虽然Prot的指南不错，但Emacs Lisp的官方手册和教程也非常清晰且严谨，不认为文档是Emacs的短板。
  - precompute则认为Prot的指南可以为Elisp新手提供简单易懂的入门介绍，填补了一些空白。

补充讨论：
• [关于动态与词法作用域的讨论]
  - ptx指出讨论中没有涉及动态和词法作用域的区别，这是与其他Lisp方言的一个重要区别，希望看到更多相关见解。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在Emacs Lisp的设计优劣和改进空间上。一方面，tikhonj认为Emacs Lisp的设计尽管不符合现代“最佳实践”，但依然非常有效；另一方面，algo_lover和mijoharas则指出了Elisp在数据结构和文档方面的不足，希望社区能进一步改进。

A big picture view of the Emacs Lisp programming language
This book, written by Protesilaos Stavrou, also known as “Prot”, provides a big picture view of the Emacs Lisp programming language.
The information furnished herein corresponds to stable version 1.0.0, released on 2025-04-12.
Official page:
https://protesilaos.com/emacs/emacs-lisp-elements
Git repository:
https://github.com/protesilaos/emacs-lisp-elements
Table of Contents
1. Getting started with Emacs Lisp
2. Evaluate Emacs Lisp
3. Side effect and return value
4. Buffers as data structures
5. Text has its own properties
6. Symbols, balanced expressions, and quoting
7. Partial evaluation inside of a list
8. Evaluation inside of a macro or special form
9. Mapping through a list of elements
10. The match data of the last search

1.
Getting started with Emacs Lisp
The purpose of this book is to provide you with a big picture view of Emacs Lisp, also known as “Elisp”. This is the programming language you use to extend Emacs. Emacs is a programmable text editor: it interprets Emacs Lisp and behaves accordingly. You can use Emacs without ever writing a single line of code: it already has lots of features. Though you can, at any time, program it to do exactly what you want by evaluating some Elisp that either you wrote yourself or got from another person, such as in the form of a package.
Programming your own text editor is both useful and fun. You can, for example, streamline a sequence of actions you keep doing by combining them in a single command that you then assign to a key binding: type the key and—bam!—perform all the intermediate tasks in one go. This makes you more efficient while it turns the editor into a comfortable working environment.
The fun part is how you go about writing the code. There are no duties you have to conform with. None! You program for the sake of programming. It is a recreational activity that expands your horizons. Plus, you cultivate your Elisp skills, which can prove helpful in the future, should you choose to modify some behaviour of Emacs.
Tinkering with Emacs is part of the experience. It teaches you to be unapologetically opinionated about how your editor works. The key is to know enough Elisp so that you do not spend too much time having fun or getting frustrated because something trivial does not work. I am writing this as a tinkerer myself with no background in computer science or neighbouring studies: I learnt Emacs Lisp through trial and error by playing around with the editor. My nominal goal was to improve certain micro-motions I was repeating over and over: I sought efficiency only to discover something much more profound. Learning to extend my editor has been a fulfilling experience and I am more productive as a result. Emacs does what I want it to do and I am happy with it.
Each chapter herein is generally short and to-the-point. Some are more friendly to beginners while others dive deeper into advanced topics. There are links between the chapters, exactly how a reference manual is supposed to be done. You may then go back and forth to find what you need.
The text you will find here is a combination of prose and code. The latter may be actual Elisp or pseudo-code which captures the underlying pattern. I encourage you to read this book either inside of Emacs or with Emacs readily available. This way, you can play around with the functions I give you, to further appreciate their nuances.
The “big picture view” approach I am adopting is about covering the concepts that I encounter frequently while working with Emacs Lisp. This book is no substitute for the Emacs Lisp Reference Manual and should by no means be treated as the source of truth for any of the Elisp forms I comment on.
Good luck and enjoy!

You type a key on your keyboard and a character is written to the current buffer. That is a function bound to a key. It actually is an
interactive
function, because you are calling it via a key binding rather than through some program. Interactive functions are known as “commands”. Though do not let the implementation detail of interactivity distract you from the fact that every single action you perform in Emacs involves

data.title: Modern Babylon: Ziggurat Skyscrapers and Hugh Ferriss' Retrofuturism
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了20世纪初建筑师如何从古代美索不达米亚汲取灵感，设计出新颖的未来摩天大楼，尤其是休·费里斯（Hugh Ferriss）的复古未来主义 vision。费里斯在其1929年作品《明日的大都市》中，通过墨水和木炭画呈现出一个金字塔式的摩天大楼景观，这些设计受到了巴比伦神话和阶梯金字塔形式的启发。他的作品影响了后来的城市规划和未来设想，如1939年纽约世界博览会的“未来世界”以及迪士尼的“明日land”。费里斯将古代美索不达米亚的建筑元素与现代城市设想结合，创造出理性规划、提升人类健康和精神幸福的未来城市蓝图。他的作品不仅预见了玻璃的广泛使用，还影响了后来的许多未来城市构想。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同建筑与影视作品、历史建筑风格以及社会问题的关联

不同观点：
• [riffraff] 认为文章遗漏了米兰中央车站（1931年建成，设计于1912年），尽管它没有摩天大楼的高度，但在风格上与巴比伦美学有相似之处，被称为“亚述-米兰风格”。他提供了地图链接供参考。

• [sans_souse] 回应了riffraff的评论，猜测米兰中央车站可能启发了1998年电影《移魂都市》（Dark City）的场景设计和氛围。

• [nkrisc] 提到芝加哥商品交易所大楼（1930年建成）与文章讨论的建筑有相似之处，尤其是图片引发的联想。

• [antonkar] 提出了一个与建筑本身无关的观点，讨论了通过直接民主方式建立一个“民主模拟多元宇宙”的可能性，似乎是在哲学或技术层面上探讨超级智能和多元宇宙的概念。

• [treetalker] 将讨论引向科幻作品，提到《星球大战》中的科洛桑（Coruscant）和绝地圣殿（Jedi Temple）的氛围与文章中的建筑有相似之处。

• [contingencies] 回到建筑与社会问题的讨论，提到悉尼的One Central Park大楼的“垂直花园”设计，并引用了一位大学社区成员的评价，指出该建筑由于高昂的房价与社会问题（如腐败和不平等）相关联。他还提到该建筑的悬挑结构曾引发市议会规划问题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中既有对历史建筑风格的比较（如米兰中央车站和芝加哥商品交易所大楼），也有对科幻作品和电影场景设计的联想（如《移魂都市》和《星球大战》）。
• [contingencies] 的评论引入了对社会问题的关注，特别是高房价和腐败对城市建筑和规划的影响，这为讨论增添了一个新的维度。
• 不同评论者从建筑风格、影视作品、哲学技术概念以及社会问题等多个角度进行了讨论，显示出多样的兴趣点和观点。

Ziggurat Skyscrapers and Hugh Ferriss’ Retrofuturism
By
Eva Miller
In the early twentieth century, architects turned to a newly discovered past to craft novel visions of the future: the ancient history of Mesopotamia. Eva Miller traces how both the mythology of Babel and reconstructions of stepped-pyramid forms influenced skyscraper design, speculative cinema in the 1910s and 20s, and, above all else, the retrofuturist dreams of Hugh Ferriss, architectural delineator extraordinaire.
Published
April 9, 2025

Illustration from the “Projected Trends” section of Hugh Ferriss’

(1929) —

In a dramatic, monochrome rendering in ink and charcoal, a fractal of pyramids and steps regenerates at different scales and angles. Vertiginous towers, the tallest outgrowing the frame, ascend from a base of tiered structures — ziggurats — rising in regular terraces. The roofs of lower blocks are dotted with miniscule trees that echo the larger, manmade shapes around them. They are the only living things visible at this scale, but an accompanying text tells us that this skyline is populated with people, citizens who enjoy the city’s elaborate roof gardens, sun porches, and open-air swimming pools.
1
This was how Hugh Ferriss imagined the future of urbanism in his treatise
Metropolis of Tomorrow
(1929). Born in St. Louis in 1899, Ferris trained as an architect and forged a career for himself in a role for which he invented his own job title: “architectural delineator”, bringing other architects’ projects to life on paper. His portfolio, now held by the Avery Art and Architecture Library at Columbia University, speaks to his proximity to numerous major works of modern architecture and engineering, with renderings of Rockefeller Center, Works Progress Administration infrastructure projects, World’s Fairs, United Nations buildings, and various mysterious, unnamed structures of his own imagination, visions swimming up to us through Ferriss’ dramatic wash of line and shadow.
2
Metropolis
is a portfolio of Ferriss’ images annotated with reflections on the work he had participated in and the architectural changes he had witnessed during recent decades, when American cities, especially his adopted home of New York, exploded upward. He made modest trend forecasts for the near future: glass, he predicted, would be huge (true); hydroplanes would be everywhere (sadly not). In the final, most memorable section of the book, he sketched a distant City of Tomorrow. This city would be planned along rational lines to maximize human health and spiritual happiness through a three-part plan with districts for art, science, and business, each centered on aesthetically appropriate superblocks.

Ferriss’ dramatic depictions of towering skyscrapers and lofty perspectives became, as media scholar Eric Gordon argues, the means by which “the image of the American urban future in the popular imagination took shape”.
4
His futurism anticipated and influenced Norman Bel Geddes, as he created his Futurama for the 1939 New York World’s Fair, the Walt Disney Company’s Tomorrowland, TV’s
The Jetsons
, and numerous other prognostications of the rational planned city, the elevated expressway, and the heliport.
5
Yet Ferriss’ forward-looking vision also repeatedly evoked the ancient past. The pyramid skyscraper that he promoted was, in his own description, a “modern ziggurat”, the monumental architectural form of ancient Mesopotamian cities. Centered in modern-day Iraq, Assyria and Babylon were geopolitical superpowers of the first millennium BCE, empires discussed in both biblical and classical traditions which had once been considered lost to the desolating force of time. Beginning in the mid-nineteenth century, the crumbled remains of ziggurat towers had inspired speculative reconstructions. 43633455.article_summary: 本文探讨了20世纪初建筑师如何从古代美索不达米亚汲取灵感，设计出新颖的未来摩天大楼，尤其是休·费里斯（Hugh Ferriss）的复古未来主义 vision。费里斯在其1929年作品《明日的大都市》中，通过墨水和木炭画呈现出一个金字塔式的摩天大楼景观，这些设计受到了巴比伦神话和阶梯金字塔形式的启发。他的作品影响了后来的城市规划和未来设想，如1939年纽约世界博览会的“未来世界”以及迪士尼的“明日land”。费里斯将古代美索不达米亚的建筑元素与现代城市设想结合，创造出理性规划、提升人类健康和精神幸福的未来城市蓝图。他的作品不仅预见了玻璃的广泛使用，还影响了后来的许多未来城市构想。

data.title: The Solid-State Shift: Reinventing the Transformer for Modern Grids
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了传统电力变压器在现代电网需求下面临的局限性，以及固态变压器（SSTs）作为解决方案的潜力。传统变压器自19世纪末以来一直是电网的核心，但面对可再生能源、电动汽车和智能电网的需求，其设计显得过时。传统变压器无法与电网通信，缺乏动态调节电压和响应电网故障的能力，且依赖油基绝缘和冷却，存在环境风险和维护难题。SSTs自1960年代起开始研究，具有紧凑、高效、智能的特点，可以解决传统变压器的不足，支持智能电网操作，如实时优化和需求响应。SSTs使用高频交流转换技术，能更灵活地适应现代电网需求，是未来电力分配和管理的革命性方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：固态变压器技术及其应用前景，包括其安全性和技术细节。

不同观点：
• [Animats] 对固态变压器接入云端的技术持怀疑态度，担心其网络安全性。他认为嵌入式网页服务器和各种通信协议（如IEEE C37.118, DNP3, Modbus TCP/RTU等）可能会导致设备被黑客攻击，尤其是在电力系统的保护继电器中应用时，存在较大风险。

• [hristov] 对固态变压器的应用前景表示乐观，特别是在全球变压器短缺的背景下。他关注技术实现细节，尤其是隔离阶段使用的高频变压器（HFT）的工作原理，提出如何在直流输入输出的情况下，通过晶体管将直流电转换为交流电，并应对高功率和高频率的挑战。

• [algo_trader] 提到Drew Baglino（前特斯拉员工）创办的新公司Heron，专注于固态变压器技术。他还提出关于中压（如6kV-10kV）的定制固态解决方案的问题，探讨是否存在不使用逆变器或传统变压器的解决方案，例如直接将400V的PV/电池转换为6kV。

• [Calwestjobs] 关注固态变压器与传统变压器在材料使用上的差异，指出新型的固态变压器在重量和材料消耗方面具有显著优势（如使用更少的铁、硅、塑料和铜）。他还提到一个图表问题，表示缺少HVAC传输线的颜色标识，并寻求反馈渠道。

补充讨论：
• 固态变压器的安全性和技术可行性是争议的焦点，尤其是在网络安全和高频高功率处理方面。
• 固态变压器的材料效率和环保优势得到认可，但具体技术实现和应用场景仍需进一步探讨。
• 固态变压器在新能源和电力转换中的潜在应用引起了关注，特别是如何有效处理中高压转换的问题。

Transformers have been the backbone of power grids for over a century, but today’s demands for renewable energy, electric vehicles, and smarter grids are exposing their limits. Enter solid-state transformers—compact, efficient, and intelligent power solutions poised to revolutionize how electricity is distributed and managed.
The push to modernize the grid is exposing critical shortcomings of a century-old workhorse—the transformer. Stemming from Michael Faraday’s groundbreaking discovery of electromagnetic induction in 1831, the first transformer systems built circa 1885 revolutionized electricity transfer, essentially by enabling the step-up of voltage for efficient long-distance transmission and subsequent step-down for safe local use. The past century has characteristically introduced more significant innovations, including the transition from single-phase to three-phase systems for higher efficiency and reduced costs in long-distance power transmission. Modern developments include ultra-high voltage designs exceeding 800 kV and innovations in high-voltage direct current (DC) converter transformers for long-distance, low-loss energy transport. Today’s transformers are incorporating advancements such as wide-bandgap semiconductors for higher efficiency, modular designs for scalability, and eco-friendly insulation materials like synthetic esters to address environmental concerns.
However, despite recent innovations, conventional transformers
remain
ill-suited to meet the dynamic demands of modern grids. Although their fundamental design provides a cost-effective and reliable method to convert voltage and insulation levels, they are
optimized
for centralized, unidirectional power systems with simple structures. At the core of their limitations, as David
Pascualy
, a technical expert in solid-state transformers (SSTs) and power electronics, explained to
POWER
, “a
normal
standard
transformer doesn’t communicate with the grid.”
Without advanced power electronics or sensors, conventional transformers cannot actively regulate voltage, mitigate harmonic distortion, or respond dynamically to grid disturbances, he said.
Additionally, their lack of integration with digital control systems and grid communication protocols prevents them from supporting intelligent grid operations, such as voltage-ampere reactive (VAR) regulation, participation in grid demand response programs, predictive maintenance, or real-time optimization.
Traditional transformers
operate
at low frequencies (50/60 Hz),
requiring
bulky cores and windings that limit scalability, reduce efficiency, and make them impractical for space-constrained applications such as urban substations or offshore wind platforms,
Pascualy
noted. Their reliance on oil-based insulation and cooling also introduces environmental risks, demands significant maintenance, and leaves them vulnerable to failures under extreme weather conditions or fluctuating loads.
SSTs: A New Breed of Transformers
To address these limitations, research into solid-state transformers (SSTs) has been ongoing since the 1960s. William McMurray, an engineer at General Electric, first proposed the concept of an “
electronic transformer
” in 1968 in a design that introduced high-frequency alternating current-to-alternating current (AC/AC) converters. The design allowed for voltage transformation using power electronic components, marking a foray away from traditional l

data.title: China just approved flying taxis – no pilot needed
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 中国民航局（CAAC）已批准亿航控股及其子公司禾怡航旅的飞行的士开始商业运营，这标志着中国在自主空中交通领域迈出了重要一步。这些两座电动飞行器拥有紧凑的设计，最高时速可达130公里，单次充电可飞行35公里或21分钟，最大载重220公斤。初期将用于旅游线路，未来计划扩展至城市及城际路线。尽管这些飞行器完全自主飞行，但仍由地面控制中心监控。其零排放设计有助于缓解交通拥堵和污染，并为智慧城市提供新方案。全球多个城市正密切关注中国的这一进展，预计到2040年城市空中交通市场规模将超1万亿美元。

43666773.article_content:
China just approved its first flying taxis for commercial passenger service. This groundbreaking move marks a significant shift in the future of urban mobility, positioning China at the forefront of autonomous air transport.
These vehicles are expected to redefine how cities tackle traffic congestion and pollution, acting as a model for future smart city infrastructure worldwide.
Official Regulatory Approval
The Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) has granted
air operator certificates
to
EHang Holdings in Guangdong
and its subsidiary
Heyi Aviation in Hefei
. These certificates are the final regulatory step needed to begin commercial operations.
This approval reflects years of testing and demonstrates the Chinese government’s increasing openness to next-gen mobility technologies.
Aircraft Overview: Compact and Capable
The newly certified two-seater aircraft features
eight arms and 16 propellers
, showcasing a compact yet powerful design. It can reach speeds of
81 mph (130 km/h)
, with a cruising speed of
62 mph (100 km/h)
.
Its small size and electric operation make it ideal for city centers where space is limited and air pollution is a growing concern.
Range and Payload
With a maximum altitude of
9,843 feet (3,000 meters)
, these air taxis can cover
22 miles (35 km)
or
21 minutes
of flight on a single charge. The aircraft can carry up to
485 pounds (220 kg)
and is equipped with
gull-wing doors
and
fixed landing gear
.
These specs make it suitable for short hops between business districts, tourism hubs, or suburban areas without requiring massive infrastructure.
Use Cases and Future Expansion
Initially, the flying taxis will operate short
tourism routes
in select cities. Over time, the service will expand to include urban and intercity routes, potentially transforming how people commute.
Authorities are exploring options to integrate the service into larger transportation networks like metro stations and airports.
Safety First: Strict Regulations in Place
While these air taxis operate without onboard pilots, companies are required to adhere to
stringent safety, maintenance, and operational standards
. Ground-based control centers will monitor flights and assist in navigation when necessary.
These regulations aim to establish public trust while ensuring a seamless transition into autonomous air mobility.
Charging Time and Battery Tech
The vehicle’s battery takes approximately
two hours
to fully charge. Battery safety, range optimization, and rapid recharge systems are integral to its real-world functionality.
Future upgrades may include battery swap stations and solar-augmented charging pads to further streamline operations.
Autonomous But Supervised
Even though the aircraft is
fully autonomous
, it will still be monitored remotely to ensure safety and smooth flight operations. This hybrid model bridges the gap between automation and human oversight.
Supervisors will have override capabilities, adding another layer of safety in case of emergencies or unexpected weather conditions.
Environmental Impact and Urban Integration
Designed with
zero-emission electric propulsion
, these air taxis represent a more sustainable alternative to cars and traditional helicopters. City planners are now evaluating how to incorporate
vertiports
for takeoffs and landings.
Dedicated air corridors and digital air traffic control systems are being developed to ensure safe and efficient integration.
Public Reception and Pilot Projects
The public response has been a mix of awe and curiosity.
Pilot tourism programs
in Guangzhou and Hefei have been met with enthusiasm, laying the groundwork for broader adoption.
Surveys indicate that nearly 60% of respondents are open to trying air taxis within the next 5 years.
Global Implications for Urban Mobility
China’s move is expected to influence
global regulators and innovators
, encouraging similar approvals in the U.S., Europe, and the Middle East. It may trigger a new wave of investment in
urban air mobility (UAM)
.
Several international aviation authorities are reportedly observing China’s deployment closely as a potential model.
Economic Boost and Market Forecast
The introduction of commercial air taxis is predicted to inject
billions of dollars
into the emerging aerial mobility sector. It will create jobs in aircraft manufacturing, operations, logistics, and smart infrastructure.
Analysts expect the UAM market to reach over
$1 trillion by 2040
, with China leading the charge.
Technological Backbone
Behind the scenes, advanced
AI flight control algorithms
,
redundant communication systems
, and
precision sensors
form the backbone of these aircraft, ensuring reliable and safe autonomous flight.
Continuous upgrades via software updates and cloud-based analytics will further enhance performance and safety.

EHang has hinted at ambitions to export this model globally. Discussions with
Dubai, Singapore, and Los Angeles

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GrapheneOS的优缺点及相关技术问题

不同观点：
• **对Google Pay不支持无线支付的担忧**：versluis提到GrapheneOS不支持Google Pay的无线支付，因为Google的integrity API限制。这导致他与荷兰银行的支付方式不兼容，并已向消费者市场管理局投诉Google和Apple在支付领域的双头垄断情况。

• **对安装速度和功能的赞赏**：JeremyBarbosa和miramba对GrapheneOS在Pixel设备上的快速安装和使用体验表示赞赏，尤其是通过浏览器直接更新系统的便捷性。miramba还提到通过Chromium安装PWAs（渐进式网络应用）作为独立于Google和Apple生态的替代方案。

• **对隐私和安全的关注**：NoImmatureAdHom和versluis强调GrapheneOS在隐私和安全方面的优势，认为它是抵抗设备监控的重要工具。NoImmatureAdHom还建议增加硬件开关以增强隐私保护。

补充讨论：
• **安装和数据迁移问题**：sureglymop提到通过WebUSB在不同Pixel设备间安装GrapheneOS的便利性，但也指出缺少数据迁移功能的问题。EffrafaxOfWug则警告在重新锁定bootloader前要慎重考虑，因为系统更新可能导致设备无法启动并丢失数据。

• **用户体验和应用兼容性**：raffael_de和m1keil关注GrapheneOS的相机质量和打车应用（如Uber、Grab、Bolt）的可用性。pinetroey则对自动通话录音功能缺失表示担忧。

• **技术和开发支持**：neodypsis询问是否有适用于Android模拟器的GrapheneOS镜像，以便进行应用测试。0x38B对比了Android和iOS的文件管理功能，认为Android在文件操作方面更具优势。tiborsaas建议恢复导航栏中的截图功能以提升用户体验。

争议焦点：
• **Google Pay和银行应用的兼容性问题**：由于Google和Apple在支付领域的双头垄断，导致GrapheneOS用户无法使用Google Pay进行无线支付，这是用户群体中主要的争议和投诉点。

总结：GrapheneOS在隐私、安全和用户自由度方面获得好评，但在支付功能、应用兼容性和数据迁移等方面存在一定的技术限制和用户困扰。

data.title: BPS is a GPS alternative that nobody's heard of
data.author: sksxihve
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在NAB展会上意外发现的一个鲜为人知的GPS替代方案——BPS（Broadcast Pulse Synchronization）。BPS是一种实验性的时序标准，可能被纳入美国ATSC 3.0广播系统的推广中。该系统通过电视信号提供精确的时间同步，精度在±10纳秒以内，能作为GPS的地面备份，尤其在媒体、电力网和5G通信等需要高精度时间的领域具有重要意义。尽管目前只有少数电视台参与BPS测试，但其潜力巨大。作者还提到在ASUS展台看到的具有内置PPS同步功能的消费级主板，并计划在后续视频中深入探讨BPS。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ATSC 3.0及广播定位系统（BPS）的技术可行性、应用场景、商业动机及与GPS的比较

不同观点：
• [Lammy] 认为ATSC 3.0的专用回传通道（Dedicated Return Channel）主要用于市场营销，质疑其隐私性和必要性，并引用文件说明行业为了经济利益推动该技术。
• [geerlingguy] 指出ATSC 3.0仍处于实验阶段，虽然其计划通过地面发射站建立独立的 timing 网络，但目前部署有限，且面临许多障碍，包括需要新硬件和消费者接受度。此外，提到ATSC 3.0的一些附加功能（如个性化广告）可能进一步影响用户隐私。
• [lxgr] 强调高功率、可靠的GNSS替代方案的迫切需求，批评美国及NATO国家取消地面导航系统，同时指出俄罗斯和中国在维持和建设类似系统。
• [keithwinstein] 认为不需要ATSC 3.0也可以实现类似的定位功能，引用2005年的Rosum技术，指出通过比较本地参考振荡器和每个电视台的相位可以实现精确定位。
• [LeoPanthera] 批评ATSC 3.0频道加密，导致不再有免费的开放标准和开源 viewer，认为这是对观众权利的侵犯。
• [RyanShook] 提供BPS的幻灯片链接，但没有深入讨论技术细节。
• [hwpythonner] 质疑BPS是否依赖特定的FM或电视信号，提出为何不使用现有的蜂窝塔进行类似操作，并讨论了蜂窝网络的时间同步和多径效应问题。
• [anonymousiam] 分享了一篇关于使用电视信号代替GPS的文章链接，作为对该技术的支持。
• [master_crab] 认为BPS可能仅在信号重叠较多的城市地区有用，在乡村和水上仍需依赖GPS。
• [kristopolous] 提供NAB网站的链接，供不想观看视频的人了解BPS。
• [teleforce] 讨论了高频测量设备的成本，并暗示软件定义无线电（SDR）可能是一个颠覆性的解决方案。
• [dieselerator] 提出使用现有蜂窝基站进行时序系统的可能性，指出蜂窝网络的广泛覆盖和相邻频段的优势。
• [skissane] 询问是否有DVB-T的等效方案。
• [rwg] 表达了对BPS的兴趣，但对其可行性持怀疑态度，指出BPS在单源接收、复杂地形下的精度、接收器复杂性和成本等方面的问题，并质疑其商业动机。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：BPS是否能作为独立的定位系统，以及其商业可行性和隐私影响。
• 技术细节：包括振荡器稳定性、多径效应、时间同步等对定位精度的影响。
• 市场接受度：消费者是否愿意为新硬件买单，以及广播公司是否有动力实施BPS。
• 对比GPS：BPS在高功率抗干扰、室内覆盖等方面的优势，但也有地理覆盖和精度上的局限。

43669308.article_content:
BPS is a GPS alternative that nobody's heard of
I came to the NAB (National Association of Broadcasters) show this year with my Dad to learn more about time in broadcast and live production.
I was expecting to learn more about grandmaster clocks, AV sync, timing in protocols like Dante, Livewire, AES67, and more—and I
have
. But then on the first day here I found this odd little corner of the building with a completely empty booth:
When you see an oscilloscope that costs 3x the value of your car on a trade show floor... well, let's just say my interest was piqued.
I looked at it, and found something interesting—the trigger was on a GPS PPS timing signal output from a u-blox GPS receiver. But the 2nd channel was monitoring
KSNV-TV
, a US television station broadcasting an
ATSC 3.0
signal.
The scope showed a PPS output (Pulse Per Second) demonstrating a pulse sync of +/- 10 ns between GPS and the TV signal output—which so happens to be
BPS
, an experimental timing standard that may be incorporated into the ATSC 3.0 rollout in the US (there are currently about 1,700 TV stations that could be upgraded).
After seeing the demo, I found out there
are
a few people who've heard of BPS... and many of them were presenting on it, as they were also the ones who were doing the initial rollout and experimentation.
ATSC 3.0 is a newer IP broadcast standard being rolled out in some countries—my own home city has two TV stations broadcasting it right now, under the 'NEXTGEN TV' moniker. But so far only a few TV stations are participating in the BPS testing.
Because accurate timing is critical in many areas, from media, to the power grid, to 5G and communications, having a reliable terrestrial backup to GPS—especially one that can be hardened against different types of jamming attempts—may be important to our economy, communications and power grid... or people like who just want to have a good time!
And speaking of time stuff at the NAB Show... can you guess what I'm pointing to in this photo, from the ASUS booth?
If you guessed built-in PPS in/out connectors on a consumer Intel motherboard that syncs to
TGPIO
(Time-Aware GPIO) on an Intel CPU... you'd be right! And if you have no clue what that means, well, I'll cover it more in depth later this year :)
Anyway, I am still learning about BPS, so I'll probably go deeper into it later in my timing series on my YouTube channel, but for now, I'll leave with with a quick video showing the demo (below), and a couple links for those who want to learn more:
More resources:
BPS / NIST time experiment results
NAB PILOT - BPS Info
UrsaNav's eLoran timing
Further reading
Time Card mini adds Pi, GPS, and OCXO to your PC
PTP and IEEE-1588 hardware timestamping on the Raspberry Pi CM4
Raspberry Pi cluster spotted inside $6k audio processor
